newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Overlapping claims delay mining approvals - Manila.
newsitem.headline: Overlapping claims delay mining approvals - Manila.

text.p: Overlapping applications for prospective mining areas may likely delay approvals for foreign firms to invest in the Philippine mining industry, the governor of the Philippine Board of Investments said on Tuesday.

BOI governor Conrado Leviste said only 11 of 100 applications for financial and technical assistance agreements (FTAA) are likely to be approved this year since the 89 other applications had problems of overlapping mining claims.
Disputes arising from overlapping applications for mining areas could adversely affect the BOI's target of 6.3 billion pesos in fresh investment from FTAAs this year, Leviste told reporters.

Department of Environment and Natural Resources undersecretary Antonio La Vina said in an earlier interview the government is expected to award new mining explorations contracts to foreign mining firms after approval in December of the revised rules for the Philippine Mining Act.
The law allows foreign firms 100 percent ownership of local mining projects.
La Vina said his department, which grants licences for FTAAs, had expected problems of overlapping mining claims by applicants.
"It's okay to wait as long as all is done the legal way since what is at stake is the national patrimony," he said.
Under the new mining law, FTAAs holders can mine up to 81,000 hectares of a designated area.
Only two firms, Arimco and Western Mining Corp, both Australian, have so far been granted FTAAs by the government. -- Manila newsroom (632) 841-89-36, fax 817-62-67
